 Vth Addl. S.C.Judge & XXIV A.C.J.M.

Petitioners have filed the petition U/sec.166 of Motor Vehicle Act, 1988, claiming compensation amount of Rs.20,00,000/- with interest from the respondent.
Petitioner died on 25.12.2024 and his LRS came on record and proceed with the petition.

Seenappa vs B.M.T.C on 2 December, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/74210315/
1 2.

Petitioners case is as Follows:
That on 30.08.2024 at about 4.40 PM, their father late Seenappa S/o. Nembappa was a pedestrian near Nadakacheri office, in Biradar Halli, wherein the driver of the BMTC Bus Reg No.KA-57-F-5147, drove it in high speed, rash and negligent manner and dashed against the Seenappa and caused the accident.
In the said accident Seenappa sustained grievous injuries.

He took first aid at East point hospital later he was shifted to MTB Hospital, wherein he took treatment as inpatient for the accidental injuries and he has spent Rs.2,00,000/- towards his medical expenses.
They stated that prior to the accident the their father was hale and healthy and he is aged about 82 years and he is working as coolie and he was earning Rs.20,000/- per month.

Further petitioners stated that the accident occurred due to the rash and negligent act of the driver of the offending vehicle which belongs to respondent and the jurisdictional police have registered Cr.No.300/2024 against the driver of the offending BMTC bus, as such respondent is liable to pay the compensation.
They prays this tribunal to award the compensation amount by allowing the petition.
3. After filing of the petition, notice served to the respondent, he appeared through their/its counsel and filed vakalath, written statement by denying the entire version of the petitioners in toto.

Respondent specifically denied the age, income and profession of the petitioner's father and contended that the alleged incident had occurred due to the negligent act of the petitioner's father and prays this Tribunal to dismiss the petition.
4. Petitioner No.1(a) examined himself as PW-1, produced and marked 12 documents, which are at Ex.P.1 to 12 and he is fully cross examined.
Respondent examined the driver of the offending vehicle as RW-1 and he is fully cross examined.
5. I have heard the arguments for the counsels appearing for both the sides.
I have perused the same along with entire records.

6. On the basis of pleadings, I have framed the following:
ISSUES 1) Whether the petitioners prove that on 30.08.2024 at about 4.40 PM, their father late Seenappa S/o. Nembappa was a pedestrian near Nadakacheri office, in Biradar Halli, wherein the driver of the BMTC Bus Reg No.KA-57-F-5147, drove it in high speed, rash and negligent manner and dashed against the Seenappa and caused the accident.
In the said accident Seenappa sustained grievous injuries as alleged in the petition?

2) Whether respondent proves accident occurred due to the negligent act of the Seenappa as contended in the written statement.?
Seenappa vs B.M.T.C on 2 December, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/74210315/
2 3) Whether the Petitioner is entitled for the compensation?

entities.text: Seenappa vs B.M.T.C on 2 December, 2025 Indian Kanoon
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
if so, what is the quantum and from whom?
4) What order or award?
PW-1 being the son of Late Seenappa, he reiterated the petition averments in his examination-in-chief affidavit.
Further Ex.P.12 are the adhaar cards of petitioners and Late Seenappa.
The aforesaid document establishes that Petitioner No.1(a to c) are the children of Late Seenappa.
Petitioners have tendered the death certificate of Late Seenappa issued by competent authority on 31.12.2024.

The said document shows that Seenappa died on 25.12.2024 and petitioners are claiming the compensation for the injuries sustained by their deceased father.
9.

Petitioners have tender the police records, that is C/copy of FIR, complaint, mahazar, sketch, IMV report, wound certificate & final report, reply notice which are at Ex.P.1 to 7 & 9.
10.
On careful perusal of the aforesaid undisputed documents it is evident that one Sangappa.

B. 
Goravar S/o Dasappa was the driver of the offending BMTC bus and the accident took place due to his rash and negligent act
. Further mahazar, sketch, IMV report, final report establishes the involvement of the offending vehicle and the negligence act of its driver.

Further Ex.P.5 is the wound certificate, Ex.P10 is the discharge summary, it reveals that the petitioner has sustained the grievous injuries that is left leg tibia fracture and he has taken treatment as an inpatient for 17 days in the MTB Hospital.

Further the aforesaid documents establishes that k-wiring, internal fixation, skin grafting was done to Seenappa on 31.08.2024 and petitioners have spent Rs.5,35,881/- for the medical expenses of their father.
11. In the cross examination of PW-1, he denied the suggestion that accident occurred due to the negligence of their father.
The alleged negligent act of the Seenappa is not specifically pleaded nor suggested to PW-1.
PW-1 deposed that the implants were removed and his father was stayable after he got discharged from the hospital.
He admit that his father died due to old age aliments.

12. In the cross examination of DW-1, he admit that final report is filed against him as per Ex.P.7 and further admit that he has not given any information / complaint stating that there is no fault on him in the alleged accident.

Seenappa vs B.M.T.C on 2 December, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/74210315/
3
13. Respondent has failed to establish their contention as contended in their statement nor elicited any material fact from the mouth of PW-1.
Accordingly respondent version cannot be accepted.
Respondent has not challenged the final report which is at Ex.P.7 and it is filed after through investigation and it cannot be ignored as it has reached the finality.
Inasmuch respondent version cannot accepted without any tantamount evidence.

14. Pecuniary damages (Medical expenses) Expenses relating to treatment, hospitalization,
Medicines, Transportation, Nourishing food and miscellaneous expenditure:
Petitioners have tender the wound certificate, discharge summary which are Ex.P7 &
10, the entry there in reveals that the petitioner's father had sustained k-wiring,
internal fixation, skin grafting was done to Seenappa on 31.08.2024 and he has taken treatment as an inpatient for 17 days in the Hospital and petitioners have spent Rs.5,35,881/- for medical expenses as per Ex.P.11.

Further for attendant charges,
transportation, nourishing food, he might have spend some amount.

Therefore, in addition to the actual medical expenses, I award Rs.20,000/- and petitioner is entitled for Rs.5,55,881/-, compensation under this head.
Loss of income during laid up period.
15. The petitioner has not substantiated his nature of work and income as alleged in the petition.

Accident took place in the year 2024, however as per notional income chart, the notional income for the year 2024 is Rs.16,500/-, and same is assessed and considered as monthly income of Late Seenappa.
Considering the accidental injuries and the treatment taken by the petitioner's father, I am of view that at-least one month, their father might have lost his income.
Therefore I award Rs.16,500/- as compensation under this head.
Loss of future earnings on account of permanent disability.
16. The petitioners have not examined the treated doctor to establish physical or functional disability of their of their father during his life time.
It is true that there is no nexus between the death of Seenappa and the accidental injuries sustained by him.

Non-Pecuniary damages (General damages) (IV)Damages for pain and sufferings and loss of amenities:
17.
It is undisputed fact that petitioner's father had sustained grievous injury.
During the hospitalization and rehabilitation period, he might have undergone lot of pain and sufferings and due to accidental injuries.
Therefore I award Rs.20,000/- under this head.

V) Loss of Amenities :-
18.
The petitioner's father might have forego certain amenities due to the accidental injuries.
Therefore I award Rs.20,000/- as compensation under this head.

Seenappa vs B.M.T.C on 2 December, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/74210315/
4 19.
Except these heads the petitioner is not entitled for compensation under any other heads.
In all the petitioner is entitled for compensation as follows:
Sl No.

Particulars Amount  1 Towards medical expenses, attendant Rs.5,55,881/-
charges, transportation, nourishing food 2 Loss of income during the laid up period Rs. 16,500/- 3 pain & sufferings Rs. 20,000/-
4 loss of amenities Rs. 20,000/-
TOTAL Rs.6,12,381/-
20.

Rate of Interest: The Hon'ble Supreme Court of India, in Sarala Verma and others V/s Delhi Transport corporation reported in (2009) 6 SCC 121, wherein it is held that it is just and proper to award interest at the rate of 6% P.a.

sentences.text: Accordingly I award the interest at the rate of 6% P.a. on the compensation amount.
21. Liability :
As per the police records the accident took place due the sole rash and negligent driving of the offending vehicle which belongs to Respondent.
It is not disputed that the respondent is the insurer of the said offending vehicle which caused the accident and the validity of the said policy is not disputed.
Accordingly respondent is liable and has to pay the compensation amount with interest to the petitioners.
Accordingly respondent is directed to pay the compensation amount along interest before this tribunal with in one month from the date of the Judgment.
Accordingly I am answering issue no.1 in the affirmative, issue no.2 in the negative and issue no.3 in partly affirmative.

22. Issue No.4; For the foregoing reason and discussion, on Issue No.1 to 3, I proceed to pass the following:
ORDER
The petition filed by the petitioners U/s.166 of Motor vehicle Act,1988, is partly allowed with cost.
Petitioners are entitled for the compensation amount of Rs.6,12,381/- with interest at the rate of 6% P.a. from the date of filing of the petition till its realization.
Respondent is directed to deposit the compensation amount with interest before this tribunal with in 30 days from the date of the judgment.
Petitioner No.1(a to c) are entitled for Rs.2,04,127/- each.
After depositing the compensation amount with interest, Cash Sheristedar is directed to release the entire amount to the petitioners by complying the mandate of circular No.39/2020 dt. 17.01.2020.
